ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The impulse response \( g(t) \) of a system, \( G \), is as shown in (a). What is the maximum value attained by the impulse response of two cascaded blocks of \( G \) as shown in (b)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side (a) shows the impulse response g(t) of system G: from t=0 to t=1 it is a rectangular pulse of height 1, and at other times it is 0. The right side (b) shows two identical G modules connected in series cascade. Reasoning: When two linear time-invariant systems are cascaded, the total impulse response equals the convolution of their respective impulse responses, so h(t)=g(t)*g(t). Since g(t) is a rectangular pulse of height 1 on the interval [0,1], the convolution value equals the overlap length of two unit intervals. Therefore h(t)=t, 0≤t≤1; h(t)=2−t, 1≤t≤2; at other times h(t)=0. This is a triangular waveform, whose peak appears at t=1, and the maximum value is 1.

method.method_draft: Represent the plotted impulse response as g(t)=u(t)−u(t−1). Transform it to G(s)=(1−e^{-s})/s. For the two cascaded blocks, square the transfer function to get the total impulse response transform. Invert or recognize the result as the convolution of two unit-width rectangles, a triangle peaking at t=1 with height 1. Therefore the maximum attained value is 1.
